articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed, avg 11 published/cycle (58 yesterday)

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active or queued, and there is no pause gate. Multi-source is the only miss, at 26% against 30%. Over the previous ten days it was 34, 30, 32, 38, 34, 34, 33, 35, 32 and 23 percent, so this is one low day on a thin post-Thanksgiving news day, not a trend. The 2026-05-09 attempt to raise multi-source by raising the politics and economy floors was reverted.
weakestArea: Multi-source is at 26%, down from 33% yesterday. The mix moved toward tech, with 16 stories against 12 yesterday, and many of them are single-outlet scoops from the Chinese tech press (Zhidx, TechNode, TMTPost) and from crypto outlets (CoinDesk) that no second outlet carries. That pulls the share down without any change in selection quality. Politics fell from 24 to 15. If multi-source stays under 30% for three days, look at the standalone cap in fetch-news-api.js before the category floors, and do not raise NewsAPI token use.
watching: Hormuz: Iran says the strait is closed and that it recovered tankers from the US Navy, the US says it disabled a ship running the blockade, and Brent is at $96 on reports of mines.
Rates: gold is at a one-year low on margin calls as rate hikes are priced in, and Tokyo core inflation at a 16-month high strengthens the case for a Bank of Japan hike.

South Africa: coalitions are re-forming in the Gauteng metros and eThekwini, the Constitutional Court ruled on the national health insurance scheme (NHI), and parliament voted on the high-seas treaty.
Myanmar: the ICJ ruled on genocide against the Rohingya in The Gambia's case.
Cyber: breaches at Air Force Cloud One, SAP and the UK DWP came in the same day as Binance reopening withdrawals after a $6.3 billion hack.
coverageGaps: The Middle East fell to 5 stories from 14 yesterday, with Hormuz carrying almost all of that coverage.
Two stories rest only on state media: the Gazprom–BOTAŞ contract (TASS) and Iran's Hormuz claim (Mehr).
context: This was a healthy day otherwise. Science recovered to 8 from 3, with seven distinct science sources (Nature, Nature Communications, New Scientist, STAT, Carbon Brief, Phys.org, UN News), US datelines were 20% and Latin America 6%, and there were no duplicates or missing datelines. All five cycles completed, averaging 1,076 seconds.
